headline: Revenue and margins climb, cash flow swings negative
summary_short: Revenue rose 14.4% y/y to $705.5M as gross margin expanded to 55.3% and operating margin nearly doubled to 8.9%; net income grew 115% to $38.7M with diluted EPS of $0.23, though operating cash flow turned negative and total cash fell 10.6% quarter over quarter.
summary_long: Sales grew 14.4% y/y to $705.5M (9.5% core), on volume +7.8%, price +1.7%, and a 4.3-point currency tailwind; both segments grew, led by Specialty Products & Technologies' clear-aligner deferred-revenue timing. Gross margin expanded to 55.3% from 54.5% and operating margin to 8.9% from 6.3% on volume leverage and SG&A discipline, partly offset by higher tariffs. Net income rose 115% to $38.7M; diluted EPS $0.23 vs $0.10. Operating cash flow turned negative (-$3.3M) on higher incentive-comp payments. Cash fell $128.9M in the quarter to $1,082.8M after the $54.4M Versah acquisition, $12.5M of capex, and $42.6M of share buybacks. No forward guidance was given in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Sales grew on higher volume, pricing, and favorable FX; margins expanded in both segments despite tariff cost pressure, while operating cash flow turned negative on incentive-compensation timing.
Sales grew on a 7.8% increase in volume and 1.7% higher pricing, plus a 4.3-point currency tailwind from a weaker U.S. dollar; core sales (ex-acquisitions/FX) grew 9.5%.
Margin expanded to 55.3% from 54.5% on higher sales volume, pricing, and favorable FX, partially offset by increased tariff costs.
SG&A fell to 42.2% of sales (from 44.0%) on operating leverage from higher sales, partly offset by continued growth investment; R&D rose to 4.3% of sales on increased R&D activity.
Net income rose as the y/y operating-profit gain plus lower interest expense outweighed higher other expense (equity-investment losses) and a higher tax expense.
EPS gains outpaced net-income growth as diluted share count fell 4.1% y/y on the ongoing stock repurchase program.
Cost of sales rose primarily on higher sales volume and increased tariff costs.
Turned negative primarily due to higher incentive-compensation payments, partially offset by higher net income and favorable timing of cash collections and vendor payments.
Cash fell in the quarter as investing outflows (Versah acquisition plus higher capex) and financing outflows (stock buybacks) exceeded operating cash generation.
Diluted share count fell as the ongoing $250M repurchase program retired shares, partially offset by dilutive stock awards.
